To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intranasal administration of oxytocin (24 IU) increases the time spent by participants looking at faces displaying neutral facial expressions, but not positive or negative expressions, compared with placebo.
oxytocin increases eye gaze to neutral facial expressions and that it differentially modulates gaze to social signals of happiness vs. anger.
oxytocin differentially affects eye gaze toward social signals of happiness versus anger.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of oxytocin in human visual social cognition.
the role of the neuropeptide oxytocin ( OT ) in the modulation of social cognition and interpersonal communication.
how social signals of happiness or anger affect the gaze behavior of the receiver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OT modulates the visual attention to social stimuli in a way that it promotes the approach of social signals and the avoidance of threat signals, which is a key aspect of social communication.

the effects of oxytocin on the visual attention toward the eyes of others are not valence-specific, but rather dependent on the social context of the situation, and that oxytocin enhances the processing of positive social signals in a situation of social approach, but decreases it in a situation of interpersonal conflict.
the oxytocin system modulates the processing of social stimuli, which is in accordance with the proposed role of oxytocin as a neuropeptide that facilitates the processing of social information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OT modulates eye gaze towards social cues and that OT modulates the processing of approach and withdrawal related social cues differently.
OT enhances eye gaze toward the social cues of happiness, but not toward the social cues for threat.
oxytocin modulates the perception of social signals of happiness but not anger.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxytocin differentially influences visual attention to positive and negative social signals.
oxytocin modulates visual attention in a valence-specific manner.
OT differentially affects gaze toward social signals, with increased gaze to positive social signals and decreased gaze to negative social signals.
